To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BGPS is a new, large, systematic, uniform survey at 1.1 mm with an angular resolution of 33'', a noise level of 11-53 mJy beam-1, and a catalog containing 8400 clump sources.
we have completed a survey of 170 deg of the Galactic Plane at 1.1 mm, with 1'' resolution, that is the largest and most sensitive millimeter-wavelength continuum survey of the Milky Way to date.
the Bolocam 1.1 mm Galactic Plane Survey has produced a catalog of 8,400 clumps with flux densities ranging from 10 to 1000 Jy, with a typical uncertainty of 15%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the structure and evolution of molecular clouds in the Milky Way, with particular attention to the role of feedback from young stars and their associated outflows.
the formation and evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions in the Galaxy.
the physical processes that shape the interstellar medium (ISM)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the largest and most uniform millimeter-wavelength Galactic Plane survey to date.
the BGPS provides a uniform and well-characterized view of the Galactic plane at 1.1 mm, which is the first large-scale survey to do so.
the BGPS is the most extensive and complete survey of the inner Galaxy at 1.1 mm to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have produced an unbiased, large-scale survey of the Galactic plane with a uniform sensitivity and resolution, which is an important resource for the astronomical community.

the BGPS provides a uniform, high-resolution view of the Galactic Plane, with a wide dynamic range in flux density and a high degree of completeness for clumps above the 11 mJy  beam–1 detection limit.
we have produced the first unbiased, large-area, high-resolution, millimeter continuum survey of the Galactic Plane.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is feasible to carry out a survey with the sensitivity and resolution of BGPS with a modest investment of observing time on a 10 m-class telescope, and that such a survey can be used for a variety of astrophysical studies.
it is feasible to perform a systematic survey of the Galactic plane in the millimeter regime.

the 1.1 mm continuum emission from dense gas is a powerful probe of star formation and interstellar structure in the Galaxy, with the potential to reveal a wealth of information about the star formation history of our Galaxy.
